product: HV transformers, HV GIS, HVDC, FACTS, MV and LV switchgear, distribution transformers, circuit breakers, ESS, DC products such as SST, SSCB and rectifiers, plus automation PLC and servo, with subsidiaries LS e-Mobility for EV relays, LS Metal, LS Sauter and LS Mecapion.
demand: Structural: US AI data center and on-site generation power build-out, Korean semiconductor and automotive capital spending, grid replacement since transmission assets average 25 years and distribution 5 to 10 years, and renewables plus ESS. Company guides to record order intake and a KRW 7000bn backlog at 2Q26.
pricing_power: Positive but not unlimited. Price increases passed through from June 2026 lifted 2Q26 operating margin to 11.3 pct, and the company claims fast delivery, about 10 months for big tech versus an industry norm near 2 years. Silver and copper moves can absorb those gains, and industry-wide capacity additions are the medium-term threat.
competition: Domestic HD Hyundai Electric, Hyosung Heavy Industries and Iljin. Global Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, Schneider Electric, Eaton and ABB, plus low-cost Chinese suppliers. Korean three-company backlog was reported at about KRW 43tn in September 2026, so all three are adding capacity into the same demand.
team: Chairman Koo Ja-kyun and CEO Chae Dae-seok. Company cites 25 consecutive years of surplus plus the PT&T institute, Korea first private KOLAS accredited lab with STL membership and the sixth largest short-circuit test capacity worldwide, as its differentiation in distribution equipment.
market_strategy: Move from distribution into transmission: HV transformer capacity to KRW 800bn in 2026 via Busan expansion and 51 pct of LS Power Solution; US local manufacturing via a Utah switchgear and breaker plant finishing 2H2027 and a planned Texas Bastrop campus; lead the AC to DC transition from a Cheonan DC factory; and use a VSC-HVDC JV with GE Vernova for the Korean West Coast Energy Highway.
bull: 2Q26 sales KRW 1577bn +32.2% YoY, operating profit KRW 179bn +64.4%, OPM 11.3%; orders +243% to KRW 2084bn, backlog KRW 7000bn +81.5%; FY26 order guidance raised to KRW 6.0-6.5tn from KRW 4tn (company 2Q26 IR, 2026-07-23).
bear: Trailing PER 79.9x, forward 57.4x on 2026-09-23; net debt KRW 806bn, debt-to-equity 172%; silver and copper drag, flat QoQ transformer margin; stock ~39% below 52-week high. No dated news after 2026-09-23.
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-28 showing order intake below the raised KRW 6.0tn annual run-rate or operating margin under 11.3%.

web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix first, price second. 2Q26 growth came from record order intake and deliveries for US and Korean data centers and on-site generation, plus domestic semiconductor capex, with a richer mix of high-margin HV transformer and switchgear work; product price increases took effect from June 2026 and lifted power-equipment margin back to normal. Sources company 2Q26 IR and broker notes.
web_suppliers: Not found in company filings. Broker notes state power-equipment margin was hit by silver and copper cost increases in 1Q26 and normalised from June 2026. Transformer inputs are grain-oriented electrical steel, copper and silver; LS ELECTRIC discloses no named suppliers and no quantified supplier constraint was found in any source read, so this is aggregator-level evidence only.
web_customers: No single-customer or top-5 concentration is disclosed. Company cites a broader customer base of US and Korean data centers plus on-site generation; brokers name US hyperscalers, Bloom Energy, Korean memory makers and KT Cloud. Electric segment overseas was 51 pct of 2Q26 sales, so US data center capex exposure is large and rising. KEPCO, construction firms and large factories are distribution customers. Aggregator-level evidence.
web_who_loses: Korean peers HD Hyundai Electric and Hyosung Heavy Industries and smaller domestic players such as Iljin Electric lose US distribution and switchgear sockets if LS ELECTRIC keeps winning. Global incumbents Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, Schneider Electric, Eaton and ABB lose the AC-centric distribution slot as buyers shift to DC. GE Vernova is both JV partner and competitor. Low-cost Chinese entrants lose the price-led segment.
web_contradicting_evidence: Valuation is the loudest disconfirmation: Naver Finance showed trailing PER 79.86x and forward PER 57.42x on 2026-09-23, with the price at KRW 207000, about 39 pct below the 52-week high of KRW 347500. 2Q26 balance sheet showed net debt widening to KRW 806bn and debt-to-equity 172 pct. Broker notes flag silver and copper cost drag and flat QoQ transformer profitability. On 2026-09-11 SK Securities cut its LS Corp target citing the fall in the LS ELECTRIC share price. Lowest analyst target is KRW 180000, below spot.
web_if_management_right: Order guidance of KRW 6.0-6.5tn converts into revenue and profit: consensus FY2026 revenue about KRW 6.5tn up 30 pct and operating profit about KRW 706bn, with FY2027 higher again. Utah switchgear and breaker plant completing 2H2027, planned Texas Bastrop campus, HV transformer capacity of KRW 800bn and new DC and ESS products extend growth and sustain the multiple.
web_if_management_wrong: Order flow stalls if US hyperscaler capex is deferred and the KRW 7tn backlog converts slower than assumed. First to break is margin, from silver and copper plus price give-back; then the balance sheet, net debt KRW 806bn and debt-to-equity 172 pct. With a forward PER near 57x the share price breaks first, and it is already about 39 pct off its high.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Suppliers of grain-oriented electrical steel and copper, such as POSCO and copper producers; switchgear and breaker component makers; US EPC and construction firms building the Utah and Texas plants; GE Vernova via the Grid X Technology JV; Bloom Energy and on-site generation providers; KT Cloud and modular data center builders; Korean peers HD Hyundai Electric and Hyosung riding the same supercycle; LS Corp as controlling holder.
